title: Check yourself: Fusion, reranking, context and recall

questions.stem: Two result lists come from indexes whose scores sit on different scales. How does the fusion method of the practice combine them?

options.text: It adds the raw scores of both indexes and sorts the totals that result
options.says: Ruled out because "the scores cannot be added" when they are on different scales.

options.text: It sums `1 / (k + rank)` for each place where an id is found
options.says: The page says "an id's score is the sum, over the lists that hold it, of `1 / (k + rank)`".

options.text: It keeps the longer list and ignores the shorter one completely
options.says: Ruled out because "an id at the top of one list and absent from the other still scores".

options.text: It multiplies each chunk's two scores together before sorting them
options.says: Ruled out because "Fusion uses only the ranks", with no multiplication of scores.

origin.section: Merging two rankings: reciprocal rank fusion

questions.stem: A reranker is given a pool of 10 chunks, and the passage with the answer is ranked 14th by the merged list. What happens?

options.text: The reranker finds it and moves it to the front of the final list
options.says: Ruled out because "reranking cannot fix a retrieval that missed".

options.text: The candidate count is raised for that question by the scorer itself
options.says: Ruled out because "the pool must be large enough to contain the answer", and a scorer has no control over it.

options.text: It is added to the candidates when its score is high enough to qualify
options.says: Ruled out because the pool is "the first `pool` ids of the merged ranking" and nothing is added to it afterwards.

options.text: It is never considered, since the scorer sees only the first ten
options.says: The page says "Only the pool takes part: a chunk outside it is never considered".

questions.stem: A company's reference material has 80,000 tokens and changes once a month. What does the write-up's rule of thumb suggest?

options.text: Build the full pipeline, since every base needs one of its own to work well
options.says: Ruled out because "A pipeline adds stages that can each fail".

options.text: Skip retrieval, and place the whole of it in a prompt that is cached
options.says: The page says "under about 200,000 tokens, put the whole knowledge base in the prompt and cache it, and skip retrieval".

options.text: Split it into 20 chunks and index only the first ones that are written
options.says: Ruled out because the guide for retrieval is to "retrieve 20 chunks rather than fewer", which is a count to retrieve and not a way to index.

options.text: Train an embedding model of its own on the text of the material
options.says: Ruled out because "The rule is about size, not quality", and it says nothing about training a model.
